Source-level local Work socket seam is implemented and author-tested as the public library boundary only. It preserves arbitrary business JSON on submit/open/request, forbids business on query/close, checks launcher token/generation and receiver, rejects long Unix paths and non-owned occupied paths, and drains accepted dispatches before close settles. It is also the single owner of the failed or unconfirmed Work receipt projection from a typed frame, shared by the CLI pre-dispatch refusal path and the receiver post-dispatch path. The CLI launcher/receiver wiring and the installed runtime consumer are delivered for the exact candidate through the installed package user smoke; teams-local-control-socket still covers only the source-level socket contract, so this entry stays partial.

The response projection parser accepts and validates the config-owned applyState:'clean'|'uncertain' field and the config error codes SOURCE_CHANGED/MIGRATION_CONFLICT/APPLY_TARGET_MISMATCH, and it now closes the config row's acceptedBinding field set: the parser admits an absent binding, an explicit null, or {primary, backup?} where each reference is exactly {providerInstanceId, modelId} as non-empty strings. D00 declares and tests one-daemon-per-file compilation, CLI override precedence and effective readback, with explicit rejection of v3 multi-agent files, unknown fields, wrong kind, duplicate identity/dataDirectory and non-loopback listeners without TLS/admission. The `--serve` entry (runtime/acp-serve.ts + cli/agentteams.mjs) is now the CLI/runtime caller for both the opencode and dsh kinds and reads this compiled intent; the DSH engine daemon is started from it through the same single-daemon path. This function stays the library contract that entry consumes.

D00 owns the capability vocabulary and the config-time accept/reject decision, and re-exports the single AcpError fault carrier instead of declaring a second one. Enforcement before a real engine side effect stays with D01/D02/D03 and is not implemented here.

Single ACP JSON-RPC 2.0 envelope and fault owner; unknown fields are preserved, illegal shapes are rejected, and no Session or control semantics are added. Transport and RPC/callback correlation are D01.

Type-only port for one engine adapter. The D02 OpenCode adapter and the D03 DSH adapter both implement this port at source level, and runtime/acp-serve.ts `engineAdapterFor` is the real serve consumer that dispatches to both kinds. D01 owns the stdio duplex and D02/D03 own the engine adapters. Declaring the port is not evidence that any engine runs.

D00 declares the version-1 negotiation frames, the master/peer RelationRole vocabulary (no subordinate) and the connection state plus history-read DTOs, and tests their parsers. Negotiation execution, connection lifecycle and history reads are owned by D05/D06 and were not implemented when D00 was written. 2026-10-14 correction: D05 delivers the negotiation execution and the connection lifecycle and D06 delivers the connection history read, so this D00 record still owns only the declarations and parsers. D00 amendment A1 (delivered by the D05 closure candidate) adds the integer policyRevision field to the context frame and the integer sourcePolicyRevision field to the propose frame, both strict positive integers with no default; the parsers refuse a missing or non-integer value, so a pre-A1 peer fails INVALID_ACP_FRAME instead of being silently accepted. D00 amendment A3 adds the required non-empty engineInstanceId field to the context frame, beside targetGeneration: it is the responder's own live engine instance, and the initiator needs it to name the required AcpChannelRef.engineInstanceId on acp.open. The parser refuses a missing, empty or non-string value with INVALID_ACP_FRAME and supplies no default. A3 changes one v1 frame additively and does not touch AgentDeclaration, which stays closed over identity/scopeId/revision/capabilities/routes.

D01 (merged 7d0bca4, fixed 75a6cf4) implements the engine-independent newline-delimited JSON AcpDuplex over an engine child's stdio, reusing the frozen AcpDuplex/AcpFrame/AcpError declarations from `packages/shared/src/acp.ts` instead of redeclaring them: original JSON-RPC id type and legal extension members are preserved, CRLF is tolerated, one frame is bounded by maxFrameBytes, transport faults are typed, and clean EOF settles as { kind: 'eof' }. acp-adapter/test-peer.mjs is a labeled test peer, not an engine and not inference evidence. Status is partial, not implemented: the D03 DSH adapter (see dsh_launch_compilation) and the D02 OpenCode adapter (see acp_engine_adapter_opencode) each supply a real EngineLaunchSpec, but this transport gate proves no engine inference by itself.

D01 implements the ACP channel/RPC/callback/Session-ownership/admission/history host. One genuine bootstrap initialize result is served under each channel's policy, D00 policy runs before every engine write or callback dispatch, history is appended before the engine effect, and an unowned permission callback is cancelled rather than approved. pendingPermissions() exposes each live callback with its controller-visible id and engine option set, channelForSession() resolves the owning channel, and openedSessions() reports only open channels. 2026-10-28 P0 adds sessionEvents(): the host projects ordered Console events from real ACP frames for user and assistant text parts, tool state, pending/resolved permissions with a stable messageId and real options, and completed or failed final events. The event buffer belongs to the owning channel and is cleared with its Sessions; it is a Console projection, not a second engine transcript source. Gate: teams-acp-l9-session-write-side.

D01 (merged 7d0bca4, fixed 75a6cf4) implements the durable execution-history store as AcpHistoryPort + HistoryReadPort: atomic temp-write plus rename, an ordered monotonic sequence, newest-first HistoryQuery paging with nextBeforeSequence, kind/agentId/sessionId filters, retention prune, and reload continuing the sequence. A corrupt or unreadable file and a failed write are typed HISTORY_UNAVAILABLE and never claim an unstored record. It holds records only: no pending/callback/task rebuild and no scheduling source. This is a source-level store gate, not installed or live evidence.

D01 (merged 7d0bca4, fixed 75a6cf4) implements the runtime child/stdio/Session owner: it writes the adapter's compiled files, resolves credential env refs with an explicit failure when no resolver is configured, spawns exactly one child, owns the stdio duplex, performs the single bootstrap initialize as the sole reader, then composes the agent-host host from the real initialize declaration. Start failure returns { kind: 'failed', fault, cleanup } and reaps the spawned child through the real EngineStopResult; cleanup is null only when no OS process exists. Stop is reentrant and escalates SIGTERM -> SIGKILL within the configured window. This is the library-level engine handle: runtime/acp-serve.ts is its only production caller and composes it with the adapter's compiled launch spec, dispatching to the opencode or DSH adapter from the configured engine kind, so teams-acp-serve-entry is partial rather than design. Both engines have a real serve consumer on this candidate.

D02 (merged candidate 1d4df3a, fixed 1af8fe5/9436aae) is the single compiler of an OpenCode EngineLaunchSpec and the only owner of OpenCode-specific engine knowledge. compileLaunch writes one managed OpenCode config plus credential env refs derived from the accepted binding and never becomes a second editable source; verifyEffective returns the model the engine itself reported through session/new and never guesses one; declaredMethods and enforceablePolicies declare what this adapter can gate. The gate command is 65/65 including four real-engine cases against the installed opencode with a local stub provider. It is source plus real-engine evidence, not installed-copy evidence, and it does not cover the D03 DSH adapter.

The one user entry for the ACP daemon. It reads one v4 agent intent (or the quick-start base intent), applies the explicit --ip/--port overrides, and refuses a non-agent daemon, an agent without a provider/model binding and a non-loopback listener that declares no [discovery] server, each with a typed fault; an unbound agent is never started on the engine default model. engineAdapterFor is the one dispatch point: the configured engine kind selects openCodeAcpAdapter or createDshEngineAdapter(), and the same code then converges a previous serve for the same dataDirectory (in-process handle first, then the durable agent-serve-state.json daemon/engine by ownership-checked explicit PID, SIGTERM then SIGKILL, typed ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE/STOP_TIMEOUT when unresponsive), starts exactly one daemon and one engine child through startAcpAgentDaemon, captures the engine's own session/new response, reports a model only when the engine returned the accepted binding, and stops by explicit signal with the real EngineStopResult; the serve state record is removed on stop and on every failed start path. D05 closure composes up to two inbound channels onto that one daemon.host: the local channel keeps the D02 plain newline-JSON loopback behaviour (and moves to 127.0.0.1:0 with the real port reported when the listener is non-loopback), and the LAN channel is the authenticated direct-WSS listener (createDirectWssListener plus the resolved admissions) whose every accepted connection goes through openTeamsIngress, so the peer wire ref never reaches the host. classifyServeListener is the one address-based classification; acpCapabilityDeclarations projects the accepted policy into the single published acp capability; and publishServeRegistration publishes the real listener route plus that capability through the existing D04 path, only after the listener is bound and the client is online, with the published revision equal to the LAN target's capabilitiesRevision. verifyReadiness still runs before either channel binds. L9 command-side composes the outbound initiator leg onto that same daemon after the listener and registration are ready: runtime/serve-egress.ts (serve_egress_owner) dials every declared peer on the daemon's own initiative, records a typed egress failure per undialable peer instead of crashing or skipping, and exposes the live rows and failures on the handle; stop closes the egress rows first, then the LAN listener, the local server, the registration client and the daemon before it removes the owned engine home. The L9 intent-side increment (2026-10-14) adds the desired-relations overlay reader on this entry: after the start dial, createRelationsIntentWatch polls the ONE durable record the control daemon writes on a named 500ms interval and makes the live egress rows match it, so the Console initiates but never carries the data path. The accepted intent stays the start snapshot and the record is only the live desired-relations overlay this daemon owns, which is how it avoids weakening D00's intent-read-once. A desired agentId the accepted intent does not declare is a typed FORBIDDEN refusal and is never dialed; a missing record is a no-op and a broken record keeps every live row, so neither crashes the daemon; stop() clears the interval before it closes the egress. The record's desired role never overrides this daemon's own accepted relations.allowed (runtime/serve-egress.ts is the one role derivation). Gate: teams-acp-l9-intent-side; real entry evidence docs/evidence/acp-l9-intent-side-20261014/black-box-intent-side.mjs. The L9 session-write-side increment (2026-10-14) adds the pending-Session-write reader on this entry: createSessionIntentWatch polls the ONE durable record the control daemon writes on the same named 500ms interval and applies each write to this daemon own host, so the Console stays the originator and is never a data relay and no control-to-agent channel is added. It applies permission.reply as a JSON-RPC response to the engine own pending session/request_permission callback, session.cancel as the session/cancel notification, and the Console body as session/prompt with the body verbatim. It applies in revision order, stops at the first write it cannot apply so order is preserved and no write is silently skipped, and keeps its own consumed watermark in its own data directory. A write that names a permission the engine no longer awaits, a Session no open channel owns, or an agentId that is not this daemon is refused typed and recorded on the handle sessionIntent failures; stop() clears the interval before it closes the host. Gate: teams-acp-l9-session-write-side; real entry evidence docs/evidence/acp-l9-session-write-side-20261014/black-box-session-write.mjs. For the DSH kind the entry honors DSH_HOME isolation, the derived profile patch, DSH_PERMISSION_MODE and DSH_TELEMETRY_DISABLED. Each adapter declares the policy keys it can enforce and the entry requires that declaration through requireEnforceablePolicies. cli/agentteams.mjs owns only flag parsing, dispatch and the runtime artifact load. Partial, not passed: the listener and the LAN channel are source-tree evidence only, there is no restart, deployed-entrypoint or cross-device receipt, and the AppSDK compile/verify gate stays blocked by the pre-existing PROJECT_SDK_VERSION_PIN_MISMATCH:0.1.0014. 2026-10-14 correction (L11): an installed-copy receipt for this entry now exists at the start-and-serve level — docs/evidence/acp-l11-installed-browser-20261014/ starts `--serve opencode` from an installed npm package (real engine child, real registry, real TLS) and serves the console host from that same install (18 checks, exit 0). It is not installed-copy engine-inference evidence: no prompt is sent through the installed entry. 2026-10-28 P0: the per-dataDirectory start lock, convergent start and retained-engine preservation (including the daemonPid=0 retained failure record) are covered by runtime/acp-serve-retained.spec.ts and the real CLI replacement black box docs/evidence/daemon-single-instance-p0/black-box-serve-replacement.mjs.

D04 (merged candidate 953d952) adds the server-owned presence lease to the existing Relay directory: the default 90s TTL matches the existing directory stale window, one unref'd sweep timer is cleared on close(), and every control operation sweeps before it answers. Expiry flips presence to offline and keeps the entry, its declaration and its generation as history, so a silently dead socket cannot stay online or be granted a connection; the control socket is left in place so a late heartbeat renews the same generation. This is a directory-presence lease, not a Session or grant lifetime change: grantTtlMs still bounds grants and expiry never terminates the socket.

D04 (merged candidate 953d952) implements the single mapping site from the frozen RegistryDaemonIntent to RelayServerOptions. resolveRegistryServerPlan is pure and reads no secret, so registry status can print a plan without a credential; loadRegistryCredentials resolves each env:/file: reference exactly once and rejects a missing, empty, line-broken or duplicate value with a typed fault, and createRegistryRelayOptions carries no secret into the plan projection. The registry reuses the TLS-only server/Relay, so a listen without tlsCertRef/tlsKeyRef fails with TLS_REQUIRED even on loopback and names REGISTRY_TLS_OPENSSL_COMMAND; the runtime never generates a certificate and never downgrades to plaintext ws. The v4 schema itself still accepts a loopback listen without TLS refs (config/daemon-intent.ts); that difference is stated in docs/design/teams-acp-daemon-config-v4.md section 3.

D04 (merged candidate 953d952) implements the client transport and health owner for automatic registration: it connects the already-selected discovery endpoint over wss, registers the AgentDeclaration, renews the presence lease with a heartbeat, and reconnects with an explicit bounded backoff on the same endpoint while keeping the original error. It never throws out of a timer, never switches servers and never holds a host process open (its retry/heartbeat timers are unref'd). It imports no config/**; the discovery plan, credential and CA bootstrap stay in runtime/registry-registration.ts. D05 adds the additive `RegistrationClient.publish` surface (R4): it carries an advanced declaration over the same online connection with the same online guard as `directory`, so a daemon publishes its real listener route plus its ACP capability without a second registry, directory or publication path. The D06 directory-projection increment (2026-10-11, previously the separate "D09" unit, now folded into D06) adds `RegistrationClient.directorySnapshot(subscribe)`, the same real scoped directory read plus the server's directory revision, which network/account-directory.ts needs to confirm a route generation; the single online guard is shared by directory/directorySnapshot/publish. It is consumed by runtime/control-process.ts createControlNetworkStatus (the control daemon's real directory readback); no second transport, server or directory store is added.

D04 (merged candidate 953d952) implements the registry daemon lifecycle behind the `agentteams registry start|status|stop --config <file> [--generation <n>]` surface. start resolves the TLS-only plan before spawning, writes a PID + startToken + generation ownership record into the daemon dataDirectory and starts exactly one detached child; a start converges a previous verified live generation by explicit PID (SIGTERM then SIGKILL, typed STOP_TIMEOUT when unresponsive); the child publishes its own readiness after the Relay listener binds, so status never fabricates running. status verifies the persisted pid against its start token, and stop kills only the matched pid after the same ownership check. There is no default config path and no second daemon start remains possible for the same config.

D04 (merged candidate 953d952) composes the config-selected registration path: resolveRegistrationPlan makes an absent [discovery] server an explicit disabled plan (no socket, exit 0, state disabled), loadRegistrationBootstrap resolves the credential and CA references, declarationForDaemon derives the AgentDeclaration from the same v4 intent, and runRegistrationProcess is the standalone long-running entry that holds one referenced keep-alive handle so a registry outage cannot make it exit silently. This is the registration library plus its standalone entry; runtime/agent-daemon.ts is untouched. 2026-10-14 correction: the earlier sentence here said no engine daemon consumes it yet; the --serve agent daemon does consume it (runtime/acp-serve.ts calls startDaemonRegistration and publishes with publishServeRegistration after the listener is bound), while runtime/agent-daemon.ts itself is still untouched. D05 adds two pure helpers (R4): listenerRouteCandidates projects the daemon's real declared agent listener into one lan RouteCandidate (a control daemon publishes none), and declarationWithPublishedSurfaces composes the listener route plus the ACP capability into the same declaration with the revision advanced by one and identity/scope preserved. No second registry, directory or route source is introduced.

D03 (frozen candidate 60bf76b) derives the DSH-native engine configuration from the accepted Teams config: the pi-ai route `teams-<providerInstanceId>` (prefixed so it cannot collide with a route the installed DSH composition already owns), the frozen protocol mapping `openai-chat` -> `openai-completions` and otherwise `openai-responses`, and a two-row profile patch (`llm-pi-ai` providers plus the `acp` provider/model row). A bearer provider contributes a `TEAMS_DSH_CREDENTIAL_<n>` env key that references the Teams credential; the secret value is never embedded. A missing provider, a disabled provider, a catalog that is not ready, a catalog with no serviceable model and a bound model the provider does not declare each fail with UNSUPPORTED_CONFIGURATION instead of falling back to a DSH shipped route. The Teams config stays the single source; no second catalog or provider binding is declared.

D03 (frozen candidate 60bf76b) compiles the one EngineLaunchSpec for kind `dsh` on the frozen packages/shared/src/engine.ts port: executable plus `--profile acp --patch <ownedDirectory>/teams-dsh-acp.patch.json`, cwd = the session workspace, `DSH_HOME` = the daemon-owned directory, `DSH_PERMISSION_MODE=workspace-write` and `DSH_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1`, with the patch file emitted mode 0600. The launch policy is asserted before any file is written or child spawned (enabled must be true, callbackExecutor must be controller, a blacklisted key must have an enforcement owner, and a required key outside the DSH surface fails as UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY). It also declares enforceablePolicies, derived from the same dshHasPolicyEnforcementOwner rule over its declared surface, so the blacklist classes the D01 host really enforces (including capability: and client-capability: keys) are accepted while a key with no enforcement owner is still refused; the adapter owns that set and the runtime never substitutes declaredMethods. It declares no second stdio transport, Session path or config source.

D03 (frozen candidate 60bf76b) proves effectiveness only from real engine output: the initialize result must name `deepseek-harness-acp` and declare all three real session capabilities, and the real `session/new` result must carry a `model` option whose `currentValue` equals `JSON.stringify([providerRoute, modelId])`; a different value fails UNSUPPORTED_CONFIGURATION and a missing `session/new` result stays explicitly unproven. The returned proof reports acceptedRevision, the primary ModelRef and the engine identity/route/option readback as its evidence source. It never assumes the derived route took effect.

D03 (frozen candidate 60bf76b) declares the DSH policy vocabulary to the frozen D00 policy owner: `method:session/set_config_option` and `callback:session/request_permission`, plus the capability/support/refusal list. The callback declaration is required because the ACP initialize result cannot advertise client methods; without it the host refuses the real engine approval request as UNSUPPORTED_METHOD before any controller sees it. This is the D03-owned defect the real-engine run found (same class as D02) and it is covered by the focused spec `declares the engine approval callback so the frozen policy admits it`. The refused surface (session/load, deletion, fork, additional directories, SSE and ACP-transport MCP, modes, commands, plans, terminals, client fs operations, elicitation) is refused explicitly rather than silently ignored.

D05 implements the execution of the D00 negotiation contract over the frozen frames only (R1): context/propose/accept/reject/confirm/ready, with no second envelope, no new frame type and no added field on transport.hello/hello_ack. Identity comes only from the authenticated transport facts supplied by the caller; a frame can never name an identity. `negotiatedAgreement` is the only way to obtain an agreement and it refuses every state that is not `agreed`. A propose that names another connection, a stale target generation, a different target capability revision, a role outside the accepted relations or an unadmitted capability is answered with a typed reject frame (CONFLICT, STALE_GENERATION, FORBIDDEN, CAPABILITY_DENIED) instead of a downgraded agreement; an accept that does not echo the proposal is refused rather than trusted. R3: sourcePolicyRevision/targetPolicyRevision are the integer accepted config revision and a non-integer value is refused as an invalid input. A silent or one-sided peer becomes a typed RESULT_UNKNOWN fault. A1: the context carries the integer policyRevision and the propose carries sourcePolicyRevision; the responder echoes sourcePolicyRevision plus its own accepted targetPolicyRevision in accept, and the initiator requires that echo before it reaches agreed, so a mismatched or missing revision is refused rather than downgraded. A3: the responder must supply a real engineInstanceId, which it emits on the context frame; the initiator records it as TeamsNegotiationState.targetEngineInstanceId when it accepts the context, exactly as it records targetGeneration, and names that value on acp.open. A responder start with an absent or empty engine instance is refused INVALID_ACP_FRAME rather than publishing a placeholder, and the production composer in network/teams-ingress.ts passes the same value it later validates in createTeamsSession, so the two can never disagree.

D05 bridges exactly one authenticated transport to the injected AcpHost and refuses to open ACP before the negotiation is agreed. R2: connectionId/channelId are this side's own transport-scoped correlation keys allocated at the receive boundary, and targetGeneration/engineInstanceId are validated against the local daemon and then rebuilt from local values before any host call, so a forged or stale generation or engine instance is refused with acp.error STALE_GENERATION and never reaches the host. D00 amendment A3 publishes the responder's own live engine instance on teams.connection.context so the initiator can name it on acp.open: the value is required and non-empty, the initiator records it as targetEngineInstanceId, and no second source is added for it. The same module now consumes that fact: an initiator session opens one outbound channel with open(), names the responder's engine instance on acp.open, refuses a non-agreed negotiation or an agreement without it, adopts the ack ref as its peer ref, keeps its own generation and engine instance on the host-facing ref because the AcpHost accepts nothing else, and refuses a mismatched ack or an unexpected frame before the ack, and releases the local host channel on every failure path, including a transport failure while sending acp.open or reading its answer. The inbound ACP frame is injected byte-for-byte; a host delivery is relayed as acp.frame unchanged; a host refusal is relayed as the single ACP JSON-RPC error envelope with the original id. The controller callback reply is restored to the engine with the original engine id, and acp.close or transport close releases the channel without restoring a callback or a prompt. The host sees only the local ref and the peer principal, never a registry address, a route, a role or a diagnostic.

D05 records and reads connection/role history behind the frozen HistoryReadPort with kind=connection only: a request-kind query is refused, not silently rewritten. It writes the frozen HistoryRecord shape and declares no extra field, so a role or target generation stays in the typed agreement instead of being flattened onto the record. Paging is newest-first with a strict beforeSequence, and the store keeps records durable across a reopen; the module declares exactly two operations (record, query) and no scheduling or pending-connection state.

D05 assembles the per-remote-agent frozen TeamsConnectionStatus from the three surfaces network already owns (account directory/route projection, registration health, live connection observations) and stores nothing. A registry outage is a health fact, not a connection fact: a lost registry never closes, downgrades or rewrites an established ready channel, and it produces one typed connection.registry-lost event instead of a connection.closed event. Half-open and role facts travel as the typed status plus typed connection-history events, never through a Session payload. A directory-known remote with no channel is reported as disconnected and never given a fabricated connection. D05 also composes the read-only status port network/teams-status.ts (TeamsStatusPort) from this projection plus the live connection ledger, the durable connection history and the current registration status; it stores nothing and is the D06 read handoff.

D05 closure owns the one inbound Teams connection lifecycle on top of an already authenticated direct-WSS connection: it runs the responder negotiation over the frozen frames, allocates this side's own transport-scoped connectionId/channelId before any host call (so the peer wire ref never reaches the AcpHost), creates the Teams session against the injected host, and records the typed connection.negotiated / channel.opened / channel.closed / connection.failed facts into the injected connection history and ledger. It adds no second envelope, no second transport and no connection state of its own; a failed negotiation records one typed connection.failed fact and throws the negotiation fault.

L9 owns the outbound initiator counterpart of teams_connection_ingress on top of an already authenticated direct-WSS connection: it runs the initiator negotiation over the frozen frames, records connection.negotiated / connection.failed into the injected connection history and ledger, wraps the injected host in a channel-lifecycle observer that writes channel.opened / channel.closed with local refs only, and calls createTeamsSession plus session.open() so the one ACP channel handshake, the inbound mapping, the delivery pump and the release rules stay in their single owner. It declares no second envelope and never sends acp.open_ack: the responder answers opens, this module starts one. It reuses createTeamsFrameTransport (teams-connection-ingress owner) and TeamsConnectionLedger instead of redeclaring them. A handshake the peer never acknowledged fails here with the typed fault and the transport is closed on the way out, so the ledger records failed and no host channel stays open. L9 command-side adds its one production caller: runtime/serve-egress.ts (serve_egress_owner) composes this module over an authenticated direct-WSS connection the daemon dialed itself.

L9 command-side owns the one production composition of the outbound initiator egress: runtime/acp-serve.ts starts one owner after the listener and registration are ready, and the owner dials every peer the accepted intent declares. connect(peerName) resolves the PeerIntent, refuses typed when the peer is unknown (FORBIDDEN), declares no explicit endpoint/admissionRef/tlsTrustRef (UNSUPPORTED_CONFIGURATION) or already has a live row (CONFLICT), reads the responder's published capability revision through the existing D04 RegistrationClient.directorySnapshot, and dials with the D05-proven buildDirectWssRoutePlan + connectDirectWssTarget pair before composing openTeamsEgress over the authenticated connection. expectedTargetGeneration is the serve entry's own published listener constant (the same value the responder's teams.connection.context echoes); the directory carries only the relay login generation, which is a different value, so it is never guessed per peer. A refused dial records a typed ServeEgressFailure and fabricates no live row; list() returns live rows only, disconnect(agentId) closes the session and transport and refuses CONFLICT when not live, and close() runs on the stop path BEFORE the host so no initiator channel outlives it. The owner declares no second transport, negotiation or session: it reuses the network owners only. Real entry evidence: docs/evidence/acp-l9-command-side-20261013/black-box-self-dial.mjs starts two real --serve daemons against a real registry and a real LAN listener and shows the dialer's own durable history recording the negotiated agreement with the declared peer, with no external initiator. The L9 intent-side increment (2026-10-14) adds this entry to the overlay reader side: runtime/acp-serve.ts createRelationsIntentWatch polls the ONE durable desired-relations record and applies the difference to this owner (connect when a desired declared peer appears, disconnect when a live peer is no longer desired), so the Console never carries the data path. A desired agentId the accepted intent does not declare is a typed FORBIDDEN refusal and is never dialed; a missing record is a no-op and a broken record keeps every live row. The record's desired role never overrides this daemon's own accepted relations.allowed, which stays the single role source. Gate: teams-acp-l9-intent-side. Real entry evidence: docs/evidence/acp-l9-intent-side-20261014/black-box-intent-side.mjs.

D05 closure exposes the read-only D06 handoff: connections() projects the live connection ledger through projectTeamsMembership, and history(query) reads the durable connection history behind the frozen HistoryReadPort. The port holds static directory/registration values plus the live ledger and stores no state of its own; it never writes, never closes a channel and never becomes a second truth for connection or registration health. D06 PART 2 consumes this port at the one control-runtime injection point (runtime/control-process.ts) instead of declaring a local alias: the control daemon projects the real connections() list, serves the real durable connection history and keeps the frozen read port read-only (before the 2026-10-14 intent-side increment it refused a connection mutation typed; since then the three A2.4 relation commands are routed to the durable desired-relations write instead of a typed refusal), and it fails with a typed absence when the port is not injected. The D06 directory-projection increment (2026-10-11, previously the separate "D09" unit, now folded into D06) keeps the owner unchanged but makes the injected directory live: runtime/control-process.ts builds one fresh createTeamsStatusPort per read over the current real D04 directory snapshot, so connections() is the real remote-peer membership of the daemon's directory instead of a static empty value. Gate: teams-acp-d06-control.

D06 owns the one control-kind daemon lifecycle and its real Console projection. The daemon starts one detached control child, binds one WebUI listener, persists one state record, stops by explicit PID and never starts an engine, registry or second daemon. createControlNetworkStatus binds the D05 status port and D04 directory read, with no second history or connection source. 2026-10-28 P0 adds the owner-less Session path: session.create writes the durable create intent and returns acceptedRevision, session.open validates a Session against the target peer's observation, and readProjection marks a live peer with a valid observation as kind=runtime, sessionCapable=true with current/no-current availability. It carries sessionEvents and pending permission options from the same observation record. Real entry evidence: docs/evidence/e562a05-webui-session-loop/black-box-session-loop.mjs passed 51/51 (r4 final) with a real control daemon, a real OpenCode-backed agent daemon and real Chrome; the r1 40/40 run remains history only. The daemon still serves only kind=connection history, and this candidate has no installed-copy, restart, deployed-entrypoint or cross-device receipt.

D06 PART 2 (D00 amendment A2.6) owns the engine-side permission decision path. projectPermissionOptions projects the engine-supplied session/request_permission options verbatim into the frozen ConsolePermissionOption vocabulary (allow_once/allow_always -> once/always, reject_once/reject_always -> reject), returns no option set when the engine offered none or an empty list, and refuses a malformed or duplicated option set with INVALID_ACP_FRAME before anything is delivered. adjudicatePermissionReply answers the engine only with an optionId the engine really offered; an unknown outcome, a selection when no options were offered, and a selection the engine never offered are each refused typed, so a missing or stale callback can never become an approval. The host never fabricates an option set and never auto-approves. Proven end to end on the real installed OpenCode engine through the real --serve listener in runtime/acp-serve.spec.ts.

D07 UI owner binding for the four discovery/networking/interaction/history pages: four data-team-page buttons, data-team-page-view, four independent state bands, data-team-observation and data-team-cancel, owner-data rendering, sessionStorage draft/page/focus persistence, engine-option-derived permission choices on both the session drawer and the notification list with no fabricated button, honest typed refusal surfacing, and real-Chrome DOM marker tests. The additive TeamsConsoleClientV1 extension keeps the canonical createConsoleHttpClient unchanged. The four page VIEWS are rendered inline by ui/teams-console/src/components/render.ts; ui/teams-console/src/components/page-networking.ts is the only extracted page module with a live consumer. Real black-box driver for the frozen WebUI HTTP contract: full pnpm build when needed, real control CLI lifecycle (start/status/stop), real HTTP probes over the authenticated WebUI listener, a served /ui/ module-graph marker check, the anonymous 401 Basic challenge, typed write-command refusals, a parser refusal for an out-of-vocabulary permission.reply, the observed bare-502 history refusal, and explicit-PID stop that releases the listener. It runs no browser: the frozen DOM marker contract is proven separately by the real-Chrome render test ui/teams-console/tests/render-d07.spec.ts.

D08 final-acceptance black box over the INSTALLED artifact: it stages the final package with the project's own producer, installs the tarball into an isolated prefix, and starts two agent daemons (opencode and dsh), one control daemon and one registry daemon from the installed CLI on the real LAN address, then exercises A01-A11. It reports per-check PASS lines plus explicit GAP lines for a boundary the candidate cannot prove and FINDING lines for an observed product defect; it never turns a gap into a pass. Two defects found by this driver were fixed on the same candidate: 44d82f7 (a control stop now closes its own listener connections) and 146824a (a control stop now keeps the durable data directory). 2026-10-14 intent-side: the one durable desired membership set per account and scope. The control daemon is the only writer and the agent daemon reads its own account and scope record. The record holds version, revision, the desired peer set and updatedAt, and every write is a CAS on revision through the same atomic durable write the config state uses (temp file plus rename, mode 0o600). A CAS mismatch is a typed REVISION_CONFLICT with the bytes untouched; a failed rename is uncertain with a fence instead of a guessed outcome; a malformed record is a typed INVALID_INPUT, UNAVAILABLE or UNSUPPORTED_VERSION throw and never a silent repair. The path is the shared convention <home>/.agentteams/relations/<accountId>/<scopeId>/relations-intent.json: the writer resolves the target account and scope from its own accepted peers and the reader resolves its own daemon.accountId and daemon.scopeId, so frozen PeerIntent gains no field and no config key is added. One record per account and scope is what gives network.membership.apply exactly one CAS fence for the whole set. 2026-10-14 session-write-side adds the sibling durable event record on this same module boundary: config/session-intent-store.ts owns the pending-Session-write record and its reader watermark, so the frozen Session write commands keep one owner without a second store.

The one durable Session-write record per target agent, and the reading daemon's own consumed watermark. The control daemon is the only writer and one agent daemon is the only reader, so the record has exactly one CAS fence and the two never share it. It holds version, a monotonic revision, the retained ordered window (at most 256 events), oldestRevision, the intents and updatedAt. 2026-10-28 P0 adds session.create to that event union: it names an agent and optional title, never a Session id, and reports only the accepted revision. The agent daemon runs session/new on its managed readiness channel, so the new Session reaches the Console through session-observation, not through a fabricated command response. A4 keeps this an event record because re-applying a Session write is unsafe; the reader keeps its own watermark and reports the honest behind refusal after a dropped window. The path remains <home>/.agentteams/sessions/<accountId>/<scopeId>/<agentId>/session-intent.json. Gate: teams-acp-l9-session-write-side.

2026-10-28 P0 extends the L10 projection from Session and permission rows to the observable Session loop. config/session-observation-store.ts still owns one record per agent at <home>/.agentteams/sessions/<accountId>/<scopeId>/<agentId>/session-observation.json. The snapshot now carries ordered Console sessionEvents, each pending permission's controller-visible id and engine-provided options, and no credential. runtime/session-observation-publisher.ts reads openedSessions(), pendingPermissions() and sessionEvents() from the one AcpHost, filters events to reported Sessions, writes only on a real change, and never serializes an unreported Session. runtime/control-process.ts readObservedSessionProjection validates and projects those rows under the owning agentId, synthesizes a stable pending event only when a stored permission row has real options but no matching event, and exposes observed live peers as kind=runtime/sessionCapable. AcpHost remains the event truth owner and the record remains a projection carrier rather than an engine transcript source. No control-to-agent channel or Console relay is added. Real entry evidence: docs/evidence/e562a05-webui-session-loop/black-box-session-loop.mjs passed 51/51 (r4 final) with real processes and Chrome. Retained: the notification row keeps a fixed Console title while the event carries the engine title, the daemon's readiness Session can still be projected, hard-crash observation staleness remains, and there is no installed-copy, restart, deployed-entrypoint or cross-device receipt. Gate: teams-acp-l10-session-projection.
